text: In eighteen fifty-two, a mechanic named Elisha Otis worked out a fix. He fixed a curved steel spring, like the ones on a wagon, to the top of the platform, and tied the rope to the middle of it. While the rope is holding the weight, it pulls the spring into a bow. The guide rails on each side got teeth, like a ratchet. If the rope breaks, the spring springs flat. Its ends shoot out into the teeth, and the platform locks in place. And here's the clever part. Nobody has to notice anything. The broken rope itself is the trigger. Engineers call that fail-safe.
